architecture.backbone: Frozen base VLA (LingBot-VLA w/o depth, ABot-M0, ACT on RoboTwin 2.0; pi0.5 on LIBERO); BCP adds only a 2-layer Transformer encoder head

It consumes VLA-derived visual-language tokens F_t, the denoised action a_t^j and the final-step action-velocity feature u_t^j for each action step, projects them into a shared d-dim space with a prepended [CLS] token, and outputs M-1 logits mapped by sigmoid to continue probabilities p_t^i. The base VLA still generates all actions; BCP only decides how many actions of the chunk to execute before replanning. Candidate horizons E = (15, 20, 25, ..., 50).

At each replanning step the expert samples K=4 action chunks from independent Gaussian initializations over a shared prefix KV cache; uncertainty U_t is the mean per-step standard deviation across samples over the translational dimensions {dx, dy, dz} of the first h executed actions. architecture.parameters: 3.3B (3B PaliGemma + 300M action expert; +4,608 register params, crop-position MLP 4->256->d_LLM, rank-32 LoRA)

eval_conditions.libero: fine-tuned; pi0 (PaliGemma 3B + 300M flow-matching action expert), post-trained with registers + uncertainty-gated cropping; note: A single unified policy is trained on the mixture of all four suites (2,000 trajectories). AtVLA lifts the pi0 baseline average from 94.2% to 98.4% and beats every listed baseline on all four suites, including VLANeXt (99.0/99.2/96.6/94.8) and pi0.5. Controlled ablations from the same initialization and data: pi0+Registers 98.8/99.0/98.0/93.1, pi0+Cropping (crops from an external VLM without embodied pre-training) 96.5/98.2/96.7/93.3. Removing the learned registers from pi0+Registers drops all four suites to 93.2/92.1/92.2/81.3, i.e. -4.45 average task-level change, showing the registers store embodied knowledge rather than merely suppressing artifacts. Register capacity saturates at four; fewer registers can fall below the pi0 baseline due to incomplete artifact absorption.
eval_conditions.simpler_env: fine-tuned; pi0 checkpoint, Google Robot embodiment with its own calibrated uncertainty threshold; note: AtVLA leads on Pick Coke Can (91.3 vs pi0 88.0) and Move Near (81.6 vs 80.3) but is only competitive on Open/Close Drawer (57.5 vs pi0 56.0, RT-1-X 59.7). The authors explain the drawer case: the cabinet occupies most of the scene, so nearly every crop preserves the whole image instead of resolving the handle or contact point, which is exactly the regime where adaptive refinement has nothing to add.
eval_conditions.real_world: fine-tuned; pi0, Franka Research 3 with a single third-person RealSense D435i; note: Not a tracked benchmark here. Custom single-view benchmark with two suites — Kitchen (Move/Grab/Pick/Long/Spatial) and Building Blocks (Stack/Edge/Spatial/Long/Grab), 20 independent experiments per cell. AtVLA scores 80/65/80/40/75 and 80/50/70/35/70 versus pi0 at 50/35/55/15/75 and 55/25/55/15/35, raising average real-world success from 46.5% to 69.0%. Largest gains are on grasping and small-object stacking, where single-view depth ambiguity hurts most.
eval_conditions.inference_cost: deployment; note: C_AtVLA = N(C_base + K*C_A + r*(C_crop + C_A)) versus C_pi0 = N(C_base + C_A). With K=4 and trigger rate r ~ 0.3, and one expert pass / crop refinement costing ~10-15% / ~20-25% of a full pi0 replanning pass, total computation is ~1.4-1.6x pi0. Attention rollout itself is nearly free because it reuses attention already computed during action sampling, and the base prefix KV cache is reused when crop tokens are appended. The gate is evaluated once per action-chunk replanning step, not per low-level control step. The threshold is calibrated per embodiment (shared across the four LIBERO suites; separate for Google Robot and Franka), initialized at the 70th percentile of the validation uncertainty distribution under a 30% trigger-rate budget.

architecture.parameters: Trainable: ACPredictor (12-layer Transformer, dmodel=1024) + FlowMatching ActionHead (16-layer DiT) only. Frozen: V-JEPA2 ViT-L/16 + Qwen3-VL-2B. architecture.action_head: Distribution-Matching Steering (DiMaS): an inference-time representation-steering wrapper for flow-matching VLAs. Extracts residual-stream representations h_{l,p,m} from the action expert at a chosen layer (second-to-last) and all flow-matching denoising steps, pairs each with a continuous behavioral feature (e.g. end-effector speed, vertical displacement). Representations are thresholded by feature quantiles into source D- (feature absent) and target D+ (feature present) distributions. Steering is learned as an optimal-transport map T (Kantorovich W2, solved via low-rank Sinkhorn from the POT package) transporting D- to D+, rather than an additive shift along a fixed linear direction. At test time, a representation is nearest-neighbor projected onto D-, gated by a linear-probe binary classifier g, and interpolated toward the transported point via a knob alpha in [0,1] (default 0.5) to trade off control strength vs. task success.

models.name: Guided-Action-Flow
models.organization: University College London

architecture.backbone: Inference-time Q-guided flow sampling wrapper around a frozen SmolVLA policy (official lerobot/smolvla_libero checkpoint via the LeRobot evaluation stack). No new VLA backbone; the base denoiser and language-vision pathway are never updated.
architecture.llm: Inherits frozen SmolVLA VLM; its text-pathway hidden states (mean-pooled over non-padding task tokens) are reused as task-description features for the critic
architecture.action_head: Frozen SmolVLA reverse-time flow-matching sampler (x_t = t*eps + (1-t)*a, integrate t=1 -> t=0) with a QGF-style value-gradient velocity update. At each denoising step the clean action is estimated as a_hat = x_t - t*v_t, a K=3 MLP critic ensemble is differentiated w.r.t. a_hat, the gradient is norm-clipped (c=1.0) and gated by ensemble disagreement m = max(m_min, exp(-alpha*sigma_Q)), then v_guided = v_t - m*clip(g,c)/beta. Subtraction (not addition) follows from the reverse-time SmolVLA convention. Critic gradients apply only to physical LIBERO action dimensions; padded dimensions are untouched.
architecture.parameters: SmolVLA base fully frozen; adds only a K=3 ensemble of MLP critics (hidden dim 768, depth 4) over flattened observation features, action chunks, and optional VLM hidden-state task features

eval_conditions.critic_targets: Sparse success-to-go y_i = gamma^(j*-i) (0 if no future success; 1 after first success); episode-level train/validation splits to avoid chunk-level trajectory leakage
eval_conditions.sensitivity: Earlier sweeps showed sensitivity to beta, critic checkpoint selection, and gating; the same mechanism can produce per-episode gains and regressions
eval_conditions.negative_result: Spatial-only multi-task critic failed to transfer: baseline 32/60 vs QGF at most 31/60 on validation; motivated task-description features + multi-family data + disagreement gating

architecture.backbone: Inference-time Q-steering wrapper applied on top of a frozen flow-matching VLA. For VLA experiments, the base flow is the public pi0.5-LIBERO checkpoint of Black et al. architecture.action_head: Inference-time Q-steered flow matching. The base velocity field v_theta(x_t, t, s) is left unchanged; at every Euler step the integrator is augmented with a critic-gradient drift v_steered = v_theta + alpha * g_t where g_t = (||v_theta|| / (||grad V_t|| + eps)) * grad V_t(x_t; s), and V_t is the log-tilt potential of the KL-regularized target pi* propto pi_beta * exp(tau * Qbar). Two variants: QPILOTS-U evaluates the critic gradient at the Tweedie-denoised endpoint x_hat_1 = x_t + (1-t) v_theta (single forward-backward pass through critic, no extra training); QPILOTS-M draws N=4 differentiable posterior samples from a learned Meta Flow Map X_hat_{0,1}(eps; t, x_t, s) and uses an MFM-G log-sum-exp Monte Carlo estimator of the posterior-tilt gradient.
architecture.parameters: 3B (frozen pi0.5 base in LIBERO setting); QPILOTS adds zero parameters for U variant and a transformer-style MFM (auxiliary network matching pi0.5's action expert depth/heads, init from pi0.5 weights) for the M variant; no updates to base flow weights

models.name: Semantic-3DGS-VLA
models.organization: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou); Midea Group

architecture.backbone: DexVLA-style policy with a Qwen2-VL vision-language backbone; four actively acquired wrist-camera RGB views feed a local Semantic-3DGS field whose geometry is initialized by a pretrained VGGT model and whose per-Gaussian semantics are distilled from CLIP and DINOv2 with SAM mask-aware pooling
architecture.action_head: ScaleDP diffusion action expert (DexVLA plug-in diffusion expert). Semantic-3DGS cues are fused into a single conditioning vector and injected only into the final five diffusion blocks B = {L-4, L-3, L-2, L-1, L} via zero-initialized projections and lightweight MLP adapters (h_l <- h_l + A_l(Proj(z_sem))). The cue set is a language-conditioned target heatmap H_t, an obstacle-aware occupancy cue O_t, a three-channel PCA rendering P_t of the distilled per-Gaussian semantic field, and a target-relative pose vector r_t = [p_obj^B, h_t] in R^4; the image cues are concatenated with the RGB observation and encoded to z_img in R^128, the pose cue to z_pose in R^128, and their sum is z_sem. The VLM backbone and all pretrained diffusion blocks stay frozen; only the semantic encoder, projection layers, late-block adapters and the embodiment-specific action head are trained. Action chunk length 15, two recent observation frames, arm joint targets (including gripper) streamed at 30 Hz over ROS.

models.name: ValueFormer
models.organization: Chef Robotics

architecture.backbone: Frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 at 518x518, applied independently to six views per frame (cam_high, cam_left_wrist, cam_right_wrist plus a cam_high gripper ROI crop and two wrist-gripper ROI crops). Only the CLS token per view is kept, so one frame yields a 6 x 1024 = 6144-dim descriptor. A ViT-B/16 224px variant and a legacy four-view (4096-dim) build are also supported; the four-view build is the substrate for the label-shape ablation.
architecture.llm: None. ValueFormer is a policy-agnostic critic and contains no language model; the supervised policy is a pi0.5-family VLA that remains unchanged.
architecture.action_head: No action head. ValueFormer emits two per-frame scalars from one forward pass: a smooth Monte Carlo value V_mc (3-layer MLP 256->512->256->1, sigmoid) for advantage estimation, and a sharp binary value V_bin (2-layer MLP 256->128->1, sigmoid) for online mistake detection. Actions are produced by the underlying pi0.5 flow-matching policy, which ValueFormer never modifies at inference; the critic influences the policy only through per-frame post-training loss weights.
architecture.parameters: 3,459,586 trainable (vision projection 1,573,120; state projection 3,840; time projection 768; positional embedding 4,096; 2-layer 4-head causal transformer 1,579,520; final LayerNorm 512; V_mc head 264,705; V_bin head 33,025). DINOv3 ViT-L/16 encoder frozen. Roughly 0.1% of the ~3.3B pi0-family policy it supervises.

eval_conditions.real_robot_sandwich_assembly: Bimanual station with two 7-DoF Trossen WidowX arms and six ingredient bins; pi0.5-family VLA prompted 'make a sandwich'; six ordered stages (bottom_bun, patty, cheese, tomato, lettuce, top_bun). All three variants train on the same 985k-frame merged set (134-episode HIL corrections with no-motion operator-pause frames excised, merged 2:1 with replayed base autonomous data) and keep the same w=9 floor on human-takeover frames; only the weight on autonomous frames of takeover episodes differs. vf-mask zeroes the 9.6% of autonomous frames V_bin flags as failing; vf-awr scales them by clip(exp(A_t / 0.3), 0.1, 9) with A_t = V_mc(t+50) - V_mc(t) (median weight 1.03, range 0.13-7.61, effective intervention gradient share 0.459 matched to the control's ~0.46). ValueFormer supplies only the per-frame training weight and is not part of the policy at inference.
eval_conditions.value_prediction: By-episode train/val split (181,421 / 31,681 samples, no frame leakage). MSE reported as a measurement only; training uses BCE throughout.
eval_conditions.label_shape_ablation: Legacy four-view single-head configuration (ViT-L/16 backbone, 32-frame/16 s window) so that only the V_mc label shape varies; evaluated on a held-out rollout set of 12 successes and 9 failures. Rollout MAE here is not comparable to the validation MAE of Table II.
eval_conditions.failure_detection: Best configuration is seq_len=16 with intervention share 0.2, deployed as a 2-seed ensemble. Lead is measured from the raw takeover flag onset, not the shifted target. Caveat stated by the authors: the held-out ground truth is itself intervention-derived (with the lambda=1.5 s reaction-lag correction), so it measures agreement with where the operator intervened rather than an independent notion of failure.
eval_conditions.serving_cost: Cost is dominated by six frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 forward passes at 518 px; the causal transformer head is sub-millisecond. Batched FP32 output is numerically identical to the per-view path (max |delta| = 3.5e-5); bf16 shifts the value output by <1e-3 with V_bin unchanged to four decimals. bf16 re-validation on the 24-episode held-out HIL set: cosine similarity to FP32 embeddings mean 0.99994 / min 0.99969, AUROC 0.943 -> 0.942, AP 0.818 -> 0.816, median lead 2.4 s unchanged; only a more sensitive trigger loses one of twenty onset episodes (95% -> 90%) at +0.2 false alarms per minute. Absolute times in Table VIII are inflated ~1.3x because the policy server was resident.
eval_conditions.task: Real-robot bimanual sandwich assembly on a live restaurant-style station; success requires all six ingredients placed correctly and the sandwich closed. Common failure modes: retry (failed grasp then recovery), double-placement (two patties), wrong-stage (scratching the cheese bin without grasping), and stall.
eval_conditions.ab_protocol: 10 trials of two consecutive sandwiches with no scene reset between them, deliberately chosen because a single sandwich from a freshly staged station is already reliably achievable and discriminates poorly; the second-sandwich rate acts as hard-example mining and is the most sensitive column.
eval_conditions.no_simulation_benchmarks: No LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin, RLBench, or RoboCasa results. Deformable and granular food (folding lettuce, sticking cheese, tipping patties) is precisely what current simulators reproduce least faithfully, so all evaluation is on real hardware.
eval_conditions.statistical_caveat: Completion difference at n=20 is within noise (Fisher exact p=0.45). A paired re-evaluation with shared initial conditions and a McNemar test is named as the power fix. The 'soft' weight variant (w = 0.1 + 0.9 V_bin) is implemented but not yet trained or evaluated.
eval_conditions.untested_paths: Three closed-loop uses of V(s) remain untested end-to-end: abort/retry gating on value drops, advantage conditioning (supplying A_t as a conditioning token rather than a loss weight), and offline filtering of low-value rollouts from the post-training set.
eval_conditions.causal_window_lag: Failures register in V_mc several seconds after the MC-label transition; the authors' visual estimate is 5-10 s for the 16 s window and roughly half that for the 8 s dual-head window. No precise measurement is reported.
